Lord Shiva is one of the primary deities in Hinduism, often represented as the destroyer of evil and the transformer in the cycle of life, death, and regeneration. The name Shiwam connects the bearer to this divine essence, symbolizing the indomitable spirit and divine touch of Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Shiwam carries deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the infinite power, grace, and divinity within oneself. The name Shiwam acts as a constant reminder of one's connection to the divine, inspiring spiritual growth, introspection, and devotion to the divine self.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shiva is the supreme god in Hinduism, representing the absolute ultimate reality or God. The name "Shiwam" is a tribute to Shiva, symbolizing the deep reverence and devotion towards him. It is a reminder of the divine presence of Shiva within us, guiding and protecting us.

historical_references.reference: The name Shiva is derived from the Sanskrit word 'shiva' which means 'auspicious' or 'beneficent'. Shiva is one of the principal deities of Hinduism and is the supreme god in Shaivism, an influential branch of Hinduism. Shiva is the god of destruction and transformation, and is often represented as the destroyer of evil and the transformer of the cycle of life, death, and rebirth.

Another belief is that the name Shiva comes from the Sanskrit word 'shiva', which means 'the one who is auspicious in the direction of north'. In Hindu scriptures, Shiva is often depicted as living in the Kailash mountain in the northern direction.
